FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Air Cargo Handling Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council. In the preparation AHM 910 AHM911 AHM 916 of this standard, assistance have been derived from the following publications: `Basic requirements for aircraft ground support equipment' issued by International Air Transport Association (IATA), Canada. `Groundsupport equipment requirements for compatability with aircraft unit load devices' issued by International Air Transport Association (IATA), Canada. `Basic requirements for ground support equipment towing interface' issued by International Air Transport Association (IATA), Canada.

In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off values should be same as that of the specified value in this standard.

AIRCRAFT-LOWER-DECKTURNTABLECONTAINER-DOLLEYFUNCTIONALREQUIREMENTS
6 CONSTRUCTION 6.1 The dolley shall consist of a rollerplatform on an adequate chassis to carry one standard container of size specified in 1. 6.2 The dolley shall have four wheels, two in the front and two at the rear, mounted on independent axles. 6.3 The geometry of the dolley steering system shall be such that when the dollies are towed in train they follow a true track. 6.4 All components of the running gear shall be within the confines~of the frame. 6.5 All steering linkages, brake system componenls or other mechanisms located beneath the dolley shall be adequately protected from damage. 6.6 All tongues, pintles and chassis frames shall be designed to take frequent impact loads. 6.7 The roller platform height shall be 508 mm. 6.8 The length of the dolley shall be adequate to avoid any interference of ULDs on two adjacent dollies. 6.9 The dolley shall have a towbar fitted at the front and a tow hitch at the rear of sufficient strength to allow for four fully loaded dollies to be towed in a train. 6.10 The towbar shall swivel in the vertical plane. Arrangement shall be made to prevent the towbar from touching the ground and from contacting the dolley in extreme positions of the towbar. 6.11 Towbar shall be painted with reflective material or flourescent paint to make the towbar visible in poor lighting conditions. 6.12 The dolley shall have adequate underclearance from any portion of the equipment to the ground when negotiating two ramps which intersect at 5'. 6.13 The platform shall provide roller surface allowing fore/aft longitudinal movement of lower deck ULDs.
1

1

SCOPE

This Indian Standard lays down the functional requirements for a towed dolley capable of moving lower-deck containers with standard base dimensions of 1 562 mm x 1 534 mm and a maximum weight of 1588 kg. 2 REFERENCES

Following Indian Standards are necessary adjunct to this standard: IS No.
7073 (Part 1) : Title

1973 7073 (Part 2) : 1983 3 DEFINITIONS

Glossary of terms relating to air cargo pallets and containers: Part 1 Air cargo pallets Glossary of terms relating to air cargo pallets and containers: Part 2 Air cargo containers

3.0 For the purpose of this standard, following terms and definitions in addition to those given in IS 7073 (Part 1) : 1973 and IS 7073 (Part 2) : 1953 shall be applicable. 3.1 Dolley An equipment capable of moving unit-loaddevices (ULD) between baggage/cargo loading facilities at passanger terminal or cargo warehouse and aircraft position and vice-versa. 4 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Thecontainer dolleyshall bedesigned for loading four fully loaded dollies at a time in a train. 4.2 The dolley shall have four-wheel running gear, pulled and steered through an integral towbar. 5 DIMENSIONS 5.1 The ~dollies shall have an overall length of 2 337 mm with an overhang on one side and 2 527 mm with two symmetrical overhangs on both sides. 5.2 The towbar shall have the eye height between 305 mm and 406 mm above the ground.

IS 14388: 1996 6.14 The platform design shall permit movement of ULDs.

manual

7.4 The brake shall be applied by placing and locking the towbar in the down position. 7.5 The brake shall be self-equalising and shall be capable of locking each wheel against a tangential force, applied at the periphery of the wheel, in either direction, which is equal to the gross weight of fully loaded trolley divided by the number of braked wheels. 7.6 The brake system shall be able to hold the above weight on a 10 percent gradient. 8 OPTIONS Following facilities may also be provided if required by the purchaser: vertical restraint devices for ULDs with base dimensions 1 194 mm x 1534 mm. Designed to allow movement of lower deck ~b) ULDs with base dimensions of 2 438 mm x 1534 mm and top dimensions of 3 180 mm x 1534 mm and a maximum weight of 2 450 kg.

6.15 In order to ease the transfer of ULDs to/from the platform and to absorb the initial impact load, lead-on rollers shall be provided that have the maximum possible diameter commensurate with design. 6.16 Guide rails 50 mm high shall be provided along both sides of the platform. 6.17 Retractable stopswithvertical restraints shall be provided at each end of the platform to firmly restrain the ULD base on the platform. 6.18 The height of the top of the restraint device, measured from the top of the roller surface shall not exceed 50 mm. 6.19 The retractable stops shall be operable by one man from both sides of the dolley. 6.20 The force required to actuate any lever or towbar shall not exceed 14 kg. 6.21 The dollies shall be designed to provide a turntable platform which accommodates the ULD base and is able to turn in a horizontal plane through 360� in either direction. 6.22 The platform shall have four locking positions at 90" increments from the normal Core/aft position and shall be possible to~end transfer the ULD at each of these positions. 6.23 It shall be possible for one man to rotate the fully loaded platform from either side of the dolley. 7 MOBIIXIY 7.1 The dollcy shall be capable of being towed at speeds up to 15 km/h. 7.2 The minimum swept radius of a train of four dollies shall not exceed 5.2 m. 7.3 The dolley shall have a parking brake.

9 MARKING Each dollcy shall be marked with the following details on a data-plate fixed on the dolley at a visible location: Manufacturer's name, initials or recogniscd trade-mark if any; b) Load carrying capacity; and c) Size of dolley. a)

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes arc needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
